steps.description:
A number with a decimal point is called a float in coding (e.g. 5.132). You can round a float number to a specific decimal point by using the round() command which works as follow:

round( value or variable to be rounded, number of decimal points )

Examples of different ways to use round(): print( round( 99.1234 ) ) displays 99

print( round( 99.1234 , 1 ) ) displays 99.1

number = 99.1234 print( round( number , 2 ) ) displays 99.12

number = 99.1234 number = round( number , 3 ) print( number ) displays 99.123

Study the above examples. Create a program that asks for a float number. Display the value rounded to a whole number (no decimal point).

Follow the test output display format.

About Python rounding: In Python, the rounding method is a little different in the way they handle numbers that are exactly halfway between two possible rounded values.

In school, you could be taught the "round half up" method, where numbers that are exactly halfway will be rounded up. For examples, 1.5 rounds to 2 and 2.5 rounds to 3.

Python uses Banker's rounding ("round half to even"), where such numbers will be rounded to the nearest even number instead. For example, both 1.5 and 2.5 will be rounded to 2.

Banker's rounding are normally used in financial and statistical sectors to improve accuracy. In this curriculum, you do not have to worry about the precision issue due to the different rounding methods.

Test Input 9.55

-2.999

0.1

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input number: 9.55 10

Example 2 Input number: -2.999 -3

Example 3 Input number: 0.1 0

Create a program that asks for a float number. Display the value rounded to 2 decimal points.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 1.532

9.5555

0.401

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input number: 1.532 1.53

Example 2 Input number: 9.5555 9.56

Example 3 Input number: 0.401 0.4

Note that for 0.401, the rounded number is 0.40. However, print() command will drop ending zeros by default so only 0.4 appears.

Body Mass Index (BMI) is a measurement of a person’s weight with respect to his or her height. It is commonly used to indicate if a person is overweight or underweight. The formula of BMI is as follows: bmi = weight / (height x height)

Create a program that asks for your name, height (m) and weight (kg). It then computes and displays your BMI, rounded up to 2 decimal places.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input Angelica Pickles 1.55 35.5

Mr Heavy 1.7 130

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter name: Angelica Pickles Enter height(m): 1.55 Enter weight(kg): 35.5 Angelica Pickles, your BMI is 14.78

Example 2 Enter name: Mr Heavy Enter height(m): 1.7 Enter weight(kg): 130 Mr Heavy, your BMI is 44.98
